source.title: Hephaestus: Improving Fundamental Agent Capabilities of Large Language Models through Continual Pre-Training
source.authors: Yu-Chen Zhuang; Jing-Feng Yang; Hao-Ming Jiang; Xin Liu; Ke-Wei Cheng; Sanket Lokegaonkar; Yi-Fan Gao; Qing Ping; Tianyi Liu; Binxuan Huang; Zheng Li; Zheng-Yang Wang; Pei Chen; Ruijie Wang; Rong-Zhi Zhang; Nasser Zalmout; Priyanka Nigam; Bing Yin; Chao Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Uses scaling-law experiments as a tool to choose the agent/text/code data mixture, but does not test the listed parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling claims or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The study reports scaling results for agent-data mixing ratio, not a direct test of the listed scaling-law versions. Figure 3 plots benchmark loss against FLOPs for different mixture ratios, but the text does not give per-run values or report an explicit small-run fit versus held-out larger-run prediction comparison. The study's claims that its curves permit extrapolation are not accompanied by such a validation.
record.test_reason: The study uses a scaling-law-style fit (loss vs agent-data ratio, L = c + kx^α) only as a tool to pick a data-mixing ratio for continual pre-training. It reports no fitted exponents, no parameter/token/compute power-law test, no held-out extrapolation check and no compute-optimal split. Figure 3 plots benchmark loss against FLOPs for several mixture ratios, but the text gives no values or fits for the FLOPs dependence. Its results therefore do not bear on any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that about a 1:1:1 agent:text:code mix (about 36% agent data) is empirically optimal, found via scaling-law experiments on small sampling models. They also conclude that continual pre-training on Hephaestus-Forge improves agent benchmarks while preserving general capabilities.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments vary agent-data mixing ratio and report benchmark loss, rather than testing loss scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies the agent-data ratio and computes benchmark loss across model sizes and compute budgets; it reports an approximately 36% aggregate optimum but no fit-choice sensitivity analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: Authors state that benchmark loss follows L = c + kx^α in agent-data ratio x, at fixed total data volume, for 45M–0.65B sampling models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In continual pre-training with fixed data volume, benchmark loss varies as a power law in the proportion of domain (agent) data in the mixture.

fits_no_version.finding: An agent-data proportion of about 36% (roughly 1:1:1 agent:text:code) is reported as optimal across Nexus, API-Bank, API-Bench and MMLU loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For agent-oriented continual pre-training, a roughly equal mix of agent, text and code data minimises combined benchmark loss.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The text does not provide fitted coefficients or exponents, per-run numeric results for the scaling curves, or an explicit held-out large-run prediction validation. The authors note computational constraints restrict validation on larger models.

untested.parts: No test of held-out loss as a power law in parameters, tokens or compute. Figure 3's loss-vs-FLOPs curves carry no reported fit or values.
Asserts that the laws extrapolate but performs no validation against larger held-out runs. The limitations section says larger models were not tested.
Data volume is fixed at 50× parameters; no compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is studied.
Continual pre-training with mixed data is a different regime, but no power-law fit in scale is reported for it.
Benchmark loss (not task accuracy) is plotted vs FLOPs without fit or values. Downstream accuracy is not related to scale.
No analysis of how fitting choices affect exponents or the compute-optimal split.

missing.what: Benchmark loss vs FLOPs (7e17–2e20) curves per mixture ratio for four benchmarks. The text gives no numbers or fits, so they cannot support a V1/V6 row, but a researcher may want to note that the curves exist.
missing.versions: none (possibly V1/V6 if values were extracted from the figure)

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The scaling-law section cites Kaplan and Hoffmann as a predictive tool and claims extrapolation 'over orders of magnitude' without testing it. The T4/uses_without_test classification is correct.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameter count, token count, or compute.
No explicit comparison of predictions fitted on smaller runs with measured losses of held-out runs orders of magnitude larger.
Does not optimize the parameter-count/token-count split at fixed compute or measure its trend with compute.
Does not compare architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
Does not test whether the same scaling-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes.
Does not test predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss as specified; the reported scaling experiments concern benchmark loss across data-mixture ratios.
Does not test how fitting choices affect the listed parameter/token/compute exponents or compute-optimal split, or whether those curves bend.

rows.subject: sampling models (aggregate; 45M to 0.65B parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the agent-data proportion while proportionally reducing text and code data, keeping total data volume fixed.
rows.measure: Benchmark loss as a function of agent-data ratio
rows.note: The text says the agent-data-ratio effect on loss follows this power-law form. It does not report fitted coefficients or exponents, or provide per-benchmark numeric values.
rows.check: This is the authors' asserted functional form for loss vs data-mixture ratio, not a power law in parameters, tokens or compute. No fitted coefficients or values are given, so 'observed' cannot be checked against any version. It belongs under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: sampling models (aggregate; 45M to 0.65B parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Selected the agent-data proportion using benchmark-loss curves while keeping total data volume fixed.

conditions.value: agent data, text data, and code data

rows.measure: Reported optimal agent-data proportion in the pre-training corpus
rows.value: approximately 36% (roughly 1:1:1 agent, text, and code data)
rows.note: This is the authors' aggregate stated optimum; separate optima by benchmark or compute setting are not reported in the text.
rows.check: This is a selection value: the chosen optimal mixing ratio of about 36% (roughly 1:1:1). It is a design choice for the study's own recipe, not a measurement of any version. It should not count as an observed result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
